- Model tends to overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model underestimates when true price is trending downward, especially in the middle-to-late horizon.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10–15 days, then gradually adjusts — suggesting lag in capturing downward momentum.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility spikes; tends to smooth out sharp drops or rises.
- Model often underestimates the true mean in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting it doesn’t fully account for mean reversion or recent trend reversal.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts stay elevated even when true price is declining, especially after a recent peak.
- Model underestimates when true price is near or below 85–88, particularly in the last 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model tends to underestimate the true price when the recent 30-day average is falling — fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model often overestimates the true price when the recent 30-day average is rising — fails to recognize upward momentum.
